mutants.description: The leaving bit of the S_RUN window is subtracted only when the window is 'full', and fullness is tested on the fault count (count == WINDOW_RUN) instead of the number of samples taken, so faulted cycles leaving a partly faulted run window are never removed from fault_count_run.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN with intermittent overcurrent (for example one faulted cycle in four over more than 16 cycles), fault_count_run_out keeps rising past the number of faulted cycles in the last 16, and window_trip asserts once the faulted cycles since S_RUN was entered reach trip_run, even though the trailing 16-cycle window holds fewer.

mutants.description: The S_RUN count is updated as 'decrement on a faulted leaving sample, else increment on a faulted entering sample', so a cycle where a faulted sample leaves and a faulted one enters decrements the count instead of holding it.
mutants.reason: With trip_run set above 16 and a sustained overcurrent in S_RUN, the run window fills to 16, and from the 17th faulted cycle on fault_count_run_out falls by one per cycle instead of staying at 16. Any pattern where a faulted cycle enters while a faulted one leaves undercounts, so window_trip is late or missing.

mutants.description: The soft-start count is updated as 'increment on a faulted entering sample, else decrement on a faulted leaving sample', forgetting the case where a faulted sample enters while a faulted one leaves, so it increments instead of holding.
mutants.reason: With trip_ss above 32 and overcurrent sustained through more than 32 soft-start cycles, fault_count_ss_out climbs past 32 (33, 34, ...) instead of holding at 32, and window_trip_SS asserts when it reaches trip_ss although a 32-cycle window can never hold that many faulted cycles.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip compares fault_count_ss for equality with trip_ss instead of 'at or above' it.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, if trip_ss is lowered below the count the soft-start window already holds, window_trip_SS stays low (and the supervisor stays in S_SS) instead of asserting at once. It also drops again if the count steps past trip_ss.

mutants.description: window_trip_SS is written as an 'any overcurrent window tripped' summary that also carries the S_RUN trip, instead of reporting only the soft-start window.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, when the run window reaches trip_run, window_trip_SS asserts together with window_trip, although the converter is not in soft start and window_trip_SS must be low outside S_SS.

mutants.description: The blanking history cp_delay advances only in S_SS and forgets S_RUN, so through S_RUN it stays frozen at the comparator history from the end of soft start.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, every run-window sample reads the frozen bit cp_delay[BLANK_CLKS-1] left from the last S_SS clocks. An overcurrent that starts in S_RUN is never counted, so window_trip never asserts. If the comparator was high at the end of soft start, every run cycle counts as faulted.

mutants.description: Blanking is applied only to the soft-start window: the S_RUN window and its count both take the live cp_sync at pwm_rise instead of the blanked cp_delay sample.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a comparator pulse at high-side turn-on (cp_sync high at pwm_rise but low BLANK_CLKS clocks before) is counted as a faulted cycle and can raise window_trip. A real overcurrent that ends just before turn-on is missed.

mutants.description: The soft-start window and its count take the blanked comparator sample from BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before high-side turn-on instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks before, so the soft-start lookback is one clock short while the run window keeps the full lookback.
mutants.reason: In S_SS, a comparator level that is high exactly BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before pwm_rise but low BLANK_CLKS clocks before (or the reverse) is counted the opposite way. This changes fault_count_ss_out and when window_trip_SS asserts.
